verification.note: Confirmed. frontend/src/components/ToolbarMenu.tsx:196-201: the trigger's onClick calls `triggerRef.current?.focus()` before `setOpen`. The call sits outside the `quiet` branch, so it runs for every shape (default, filled, quiet). The comment at :197-198 says the Escape handler on the wrapper box (:186-192) relies on it. TargetMenu.addonKey.test.tsx:179 sends Escape to `document.activeElement`. The spec's touch point (docs/specs/addon-app-header.md:249) lists only the `quiet` shape for ToolbarMenu.tsx, and the spec never mentions focus. For the user, the effect is that the trigger now gets focus on click in browsers that don't do this themselves (macOS Safari), so Escape closes the menu there. This looks harmless or even helpful, but it does change behaviour for every ToolbarMenu caller that I15 covers.

specification_compliance: The touched files in r1/classification.json include ToolbarMenu.tsx, componentFixtureParity.test.tsx, VideoApp.states.test.tsx, VideoAppHeader.tsx and ReadingAppHeader.tsx. Apart from ToolbarMenu's `quiet` shape, the touch points do not name these changes.

The touch point for the shelf pages' sort menus covers both LibraryControls.tsx files: the `quiet` prop on SortChoiceMenu (videoapp/LibraryControls.tsx:52) and on ReadingSortMenu (readingapp/LibraryControls.tsx:174) defaults to false.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Clicking any ToolbarMenu trigger now focuses it explicitly (ToolbarMenu.tsx:199) for every shape. In browsers that don't focus a button on click, Escape now closes the menu where before it may not have.
regression_risks: The explicit focus on click reaches every ToolbarMenu caller. I15 counts only visual drawing, so this change is outside its check.
test_coverage: TargetMenu.addonKey.test.tsx:179 depends on the trigger being focused when Escape is sent to `document.activeElement`.
